SECTION: RCD01 §9 — the minimum claimable reproduction criterion
STRONG_SELF_REPRODUCTION: R0 and R1 and R2 and R3

ANSWERS.what_exactly_is_the_parent_system: the spatial centre, under the frozen toroidal single-linkage partition of Y-occupied cells, whose centroid is closest to the single pre-separation centroid at the separation step. It is an ORGANISATION, not a particle: no founder identity is required.
ANSWERS.what_exactly_is_the_daughter_system: the other component at the separation step, tracked forward by maximum cell overlap then minimum toroidal centroid distance
ANSWERS.when_is_the_daughter_born: at the separation step t0, the first step at which the frozen classifier returns exactly two spatial centres
ANSWERS.when_is_it_mature: at t0 + T_PRIMARY_STEPS - 1 = t0 + 249, the frozen FDFLT01 maturation event, T_PRIMARY_STEPS being ceil of one e-folding of the slowest mode of the X operator
ANSWERS.what_makes_it_independent: its qualified local X response survives removal of the parent centre for a physically derived hold interval; nothing weaker is causal
ANSWERS.what_material_turnover_is_required: its local X mass at maturation must exceed the exact 95% binomial upper bound on the number of pre-separation molecules surviving anywhere in the world; no percentage is chosen
ANSWERS.does_the_parent_need_to_survive: no. The criterion is about the daughter's independence from the parent, not the parent's persistence. Requiring parent survival would import the founder-survival gate that FLCR01 rejected.
ANSWERS.does_the_daughter_need_reproductive_comp: not for the MINIMAL claim. Requiring it would make the definition regress infinitely. It is the STRONG claim.

WHY_NOT: organisation-level identity is sufficient at every step of the criterion, and particle identity was already shown irrelevant by FLCR01
REQUIRED_BEFORE_ANY_TEST: a declared deterministic tie-break in the parent/daughter rule — RCD01 found one world of 192 where the two components are EXACTLY equidistant from the pre-separation centroid and the rule is silent
